articles.author: Steve Luck

articles.title: Technical Parameters and Feedback Control for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Enhancement by Focused Ultrasound
articles.content: Focused ultrasound combined with intravenously infused microbubbles has been shown to effectively enhance the permeability of the blood-brain barrier, facilitating drug delivery to the brain. A wide range of technical parameters has been evaluated through preclinical studies and clinical trials. Generally, a low frequency between 200 and 300 kHz is preferred for the transcranial approach, while 1 MHz is used in implantable devices. Standard parameters include a burst length of 5 to 10 ms, a pulse repetition frequency of 0.2 to 10 Hz, and sonication durations of 90 to 180 seconds. A pressure magnitude around 0.46 mechanical index appears to be near the threshold for BBB permeability enhancement at standard microbubble dosage without causing hemorrhage. Various microbubble and nanobubble types have been tested at different doses, which in principle can be normalized by gas volume. Control methods that use harmonic emmisions for power feedback have been proposed to enhance consistency and account for patient variability, and these methods are currently being tested in several clinical trials.

articles.title: Decoding Spikes From Multiunit Data
articles.content: Communication and control in biological systems is mediated by the timing of discharges –spikes– from excitable cells such as neurons and muscle fibers. Each spike is associated to a characteristic waveform that can be captured by sensors. The waveform's characteristics depend on the cell's biophysical properties and the recording modality. Depending on the technique, e.g., electrical recordings with electrodes, optical imaging, ultrasound, the observed signals are mixtures of waveforms emitted from active cells/sources (multiunit data/signals). Recovering the timing and identity of these sources (multiunit or spike decoding) is central to neuroscience, clinical diagnostics, and neural interfacing, yet it remains challenging due to waveform superposition, non-stationarity, limited training labels, and the computational demands of high-density recordings. This review provides a unified methodological perspective on spike decoding by formalizing the problem as a sparse source separation task under a convolutive mixing model. Rather than organizing the literature by application domain, we group and critically compare methods by their underlying principles: classical spike sorting, Bayesian and probabilistic inference, blind source separation, and data-driven approaches, including deep learning and hybrid schemes. For each class of methods, we present the core mathematical formulation and algorithmic strategies and discuss assumptions and limitations. Our synthesis highlights parallels in signal processing across physical recording modalities and clarifies when and why particular approaches succeed or fail. By bridging previously compartmentalized literature, this survey aims to accelerate crosspollination of ideas between application areas and to provide a roadmap for selecting, adapting, and advancing decoding methods across diverse multiunit recording modalities.

articles.title: Anti-GABAB receptor autoimmunity causes cognitive decline by presynaptic pathology
articles.content: The GABAB receptor is a central regulator of neuronal transmission and excitability by pre- and postsynaptic mechanisms. Its dysfunction causes severe neurological disease, but the underlying pathomechanisms remain elusive. Here, we exploit a distinct CNS autoimmune disorder in which patients develop specific autoantibodies against GABAB receptors causing autoimmune encephalitis with severe memory dysfunction and epilepsy. We demonstrate that human autoantibodies target the sushi-domains of the GABAB receptor B1a subunit and the B2 subunit and interfere with presynaptic signaling. This specific presynaptic pathology results from exclusive functional antagonism of the B1a subunit and disrupts short- and long-term synaptic plasticity, abnormally amplifies hippocampal network oscillations and coupling in vivo, and ultimately impairs memory consolidation. Our results demonstrate that autoimmune presynaptic pathomechanisms alone are sufficient to interfere with memory processing, thus defining a causal link between molecular GABAB receptor disturbance, synaptic pathology, circuit dysfunction, and dementia distinct from classical neurodegenerative processes.
articles.author: Sell, J., Loi, E. A., Rahmati, V., Majoros, M., Kirmann, T., Haselmann, H., Stumpf, A., Goetz, T., Franke, C., Leypold, F., Jarius, S., Melzer, N., Lewerenz, J., Kunze, A., Pruess, H., Schmitz, D., Hallermann, S. J., Schmidt-Hieber, C., Kornau, H.-C., Geis, C.

articles.title: Nanoarchitecture of the presynaptic cell adhesion molecule PTPσ in relation to prospective vesicle fusion sites and postsynaptic NMDA receptors
articles.content: Protein organization at individual synapses tunes synaptic function. Presynaptic release-regulating proteins and postsynaptic receptors each concentrate into subsynaptic nanoclusters, and their precise alignment across the cleft into nanocolumns can maximize receptor activation following vesicle fusion. However, both the molecular organization defining presynaptic fusion sites and the mechanisms by which they are spatially coordinated with postsynaptic complexes remains unclear. Presynaptic transmembrane cell adhesion molecules may mediate both processes as they could simultaneously anchor cytosolic fusion machinery to the presynaptic membrane and bridge the cleft to coordinate PSD organization. The LAR-RPTP family member PTP{sigma} is an important possibility, as its trans-synaptic interactors that bind PSD-95 are associated with NMDAR dysfunction, suggesting PTP{sigma} may coordinate NMDAR positioning. However, PTP{sigma}'s subsynaptic organization has not been determined. Here, we investigate the cellular expression and subsynaptic nano-organization of endogenous PTP{sigma} in cultured rat hippocampal neurons. We find that PTP{sigma} is enriched at most excitatory synapses, but unexpectedly, PTP{sigma} nanoclusters do not colocalize with the vesicle priming protein Munc13-1. Instead, they adopt a stereotyped position adjacent to this machinery, without preferential association with sites in nanocolumns. PTP{sigma} nanoclusters also lie offset from postsynaptic NMDA receptors, mirroring their relationship to vesicle fusion sites, yet the presence of PTP{sigma} at a nanocolumn does not predict NMDAR abundance. Together, these findings suggest that PTP{sigma} does not directly coordinate release site - NMDAR alignment but instead occupies defined nanoscale positions adjacent to vesicle fusion sites, potentially helping to shape or stabilize the vesicle priming landscape of the active zone.
articles.author: DeMarco Hibbs, E. M., Mitias, S., Aitken, R., Levy, A. D., Blanpied, T. A.

articles.title: Cellular and mitochondrial correlates of regional glucose metabolism in the human cortex
articles.content: Regional differences in human brain glucose metabolism reflect local energy demands, but their cellular and mitochondrial determinants remain unclear. We combined [18F]FDG positron emission tomography in healthy human participants with estimates of cellular composition and mitochondrial density to unravel (sub)cellular correlates of heterogeneity in brain glucose metabolism. By correcting for RNA content and differential gene expression due to postmortem sampling, we addressed methodological shortcomings in multimodal neuroimaging integration. We introduce transcriptionally derived cytoarchitectonic maps of the human cortex that are consistent with histological findings, providing a biologically grounded framework for relating in vivo neuroimaging signals. Accordingly, mitochondrial distribution showed strong association with the intrinsic energy requirements at resting state. In contrast, relations between metabolism and neuronal composition were driven by sensory input and mitochondria-sparse thin-axon neurons, suggesting that stimulation-induced energy demand is met rather by neuronal processes that are independent of mitochondrial abundance to maintain efficient information processing.

articles.title: Prefrontal cortical morphometric covariance and cognitive task performance in healthy young adults: an exploratory analysis of Human Connectome Project data
articles.content: The prefrontal cortex (PFC) is implicated in many cognitive tasks, including working memory, reward-based decision-making, executive control, and metacognition. This exploratory analysis investigated whether individual expression of PFC cortical thickness and surface area covariance components is associated with cognitive task performance. The sample comprised Human Connectome Project (HCP) MRI data from 743 healthy adults (age 22–36+). Oblimin-rotated principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to residualized thickness and surface area for 22 PFC regions, controlling for age, sex, and ICV. Component scores were entered as predictors in separate regression models for the Flanker Age-Adjusted Score (inhibitory control), the Gambling RT Difference (RT for the same “larger” guess in reward minus punishment blocks), and 2-Back median RT (working memory speed). Parallel analysis favored two thickness components; a prespecified three-component solution (Global/Lateral PFC, RC1; Orbitofrontal, RC2; Anterior Cingulate, RC3; 53.7% of variance) was retained by decision, and RC1 and RC2 were only moderately stable across bootstrap resamples. RC1 was nominally associated with lower Flanker scores (β = −0.103, p = 0.027), opposite to the predicted direction, and RC2 with a smaller Gambling RT Difference (β = −0.103, p = 0.025); neither survived false discovery rate (FDR) correction (q = 0.054). In uncorrected models added at review, whole-cortex mean thickness alone robustly predicted Flanker scores but not the Gambling RT Difference; neither component association survived regressing mean thickness out before PCA. In surface area analyses, greater orbitofrontal surface area (AC2) was associated with faster 2-Back RT (β = −0.125, p = 0.003; q = 0.032 across 12 surface area tests and 0.064 across all 24 component tests), not explained by a speed-accuracy tradeoff. This unpredicted association persisted in most sensitivity analyses but was attenuated and non-significant when total surface area was regressed out before PCA (β = −0.065, p = 0.078). In conclusion, no prefrontal-specific association was robust. Global cortical thickness accounts for the Flanker association more parsimoniously, the Gambling RT Difference association was not robust under either account, and the orbitofrontal surface area association could not be separated from global surface area; all associations require replication.
articles.author: Roman Chivers

articles.title: CEP-MI: a novel cue-execution dual-stage motor imagery paradigm with PGCANet decoding architecture
articles.content: BackgroundMotor imagery-based brain-computer interface (MI-BCI) holds great potential in neurorehabilitation and motor assistance. Data quality and motor intention decoding effectiveness are closely associated with participants’ engagement. However, previous MI tasks ignored active engagement regulation, and neural mechanisms underlying the transition from motor imagery to execution remain unclear, with limited relevant research. Conventional separate-trial designs cannot capture continuous brain dynamics from imagery to execution and cannot objectively evaluate subject engagement, which hinders mechanism exploration and stable decoding.MethodsTo address these paradigm-related limitations, a novel cue-execution MI paradigm (CEP-MI) with countdown anchors was designed to quantify engagement. Motor execution sessions were added post-imagery to reveal neural differences during the transition and identify movement-related brain activities. Meanwhile, to boost MI-EEG decoding performance, a collaborative decoding architecture (PGCANet) integrating prior guidance and channel awareness was proposed, with dual branches and consistency constraint loss for decision fusion.ResultsCEP-MI effectively quantifies participant engagement, and PGCANet achieves superior decoding performance compared to traditional algorithms and advanced models, with the optimal average accuracy reaching 85.77% in binary classification and 82.47% in quadruple classification.ConclusionTargeting the above-mentioned research gaps, the CEP-MI paradigm provides valuable insights into the imagery-execution transition mechanism. PGCANet enhances MI decoding accuracy via multi-branch collaboration, laying a foundation for MI-BCI’s clinical application in neurorehabilitation.SignificanceThis study introduces a novel paradigm and collaborative architecture that significantly advance MI-BCI decoding accuracy and engagement quantification, and helps to promote its clinical application in neurorehabilitation.
articles.author: Caili Gong

articles.title: Explainable fMRI decoding reveals neurobiological signatures of emotional arousal complementary to traditional analyses
articles.content: Objective. Understanding how emotional arousal is represented in the brain is fundamental for elucidating affective regulation and its alterations in autism spectrum disorder. Classical neuroimaging approaches, such as the general linear model (GLM), have provided important insights into emotional processing. However, the extent to which data-driven decoding and traditional model-based analyses provide complementary information about emotional arousal remains unclear. Approach. We introduce an explainable artificial intelligence framework that combines the lightweight functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) decoder (fMRINet) with Deep Learning Important FeaTures to derive data-driven neurobiological signatures of emotional arousal. The framework enables interpretation of spatiotemporal neural contributions during emotional processing. We applied the framework to fMRI data acquired while neurotypically and autistic participants viewed naturalistic emotional videos and compared the resulting signatures with categorical and parametric GLM analyses. Main results. The framework identified distinct spatiotemporal neurobiological signatures associated with emotional arousal. Neurotypical participants engaged a distributed perceptual-limbic-prefrontal network under high arousal and frontoparietal executive regions under low arousal. In contrast, autistic participants exhibited a more spatially restricted and posterior-biased pattern under high arousal, with reduced ventromedial prefrontal and limbic contributions, while low-arousal patterns resembled typically developing, suggesting preserved executive mechanisms during low-arousal processing. The GLM analyses revealed partly convergent and partly distinct findings: categorical GLM detected no significant group differences, whereas parametric GLM identified widespread cortical-subcortical modulation in neurotypical individuals and cerebellar-restricted effects in autistic, consistent with compensatory reliance on motor-timing circuits. Significance. The proposed framework provides an interpretable, data-driven perspective on emotional processing and reveals neurobiologically plausible patterns consistent with existing literature. Together, the explainable decoding and GLM results highlight complementary aspects of emotional arousal processing, suggesting that explainable decoding approaches may provide additional insights alongside traditional model-based neuroimaging analyses.

articles.content: Motor cortical high-gamma oscillations (60-90 Hz) occur at movement onset and are spatially focused over the contralateral primary motor cortex. articles.content: The choices we make during the recording, preprocessing and analysis of event-related potentials (ERP) data can affect study outcomes. articles.title: Eye-Tracking-BIDS: the Brain Imaging Data Structure extended to gaze position and pupil data
articles.content: The Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) is a widely adopted, community-driven standard to organize neuroimaging data and metadata. Although numerous extensions have been developed to incrementally extend coverage to new modalities and data types, an unambiguous, granular specification for eye-tracking recordings is lacking.
